title: appbox intake answers
description: What the intake engine ELICITS — never generates. Each field records who supplied it: 'client' (stated by the client), 'founder' (stated by the founder), or 'inferred' (could not be elicited; a placeholder the emitted brief MUST flag for confirmation). The engine turns a document conforming to this schema into docs/intake/brief.md plus a seeded registry.json. Recording content here that was not elicited is the single violation this schema exists to prevent (architecture §22: intake elicits; it does not generate).

product.description: One line: what the app is.

audience.description: Who the app is for, in JTBD format: 'When [situation], I want [motivation], so I can [outcome]'.

appMustDo.description: The (up to three) things the app must do. Elicited, not invented.

existingSystems.description: What exists today that this replaces or integrates with.

targets.description: Platform-only targets (architecture §11); viewports derive. value is an array of platform strings.

locales.description: Target locales (BCP-47-ish, e.g. en, pl — not regex-validated). Rendered immediately after Targets. Optional.

brand.description: Name, colour, voice — only if the client stated one.

direction.description: Design direction: adjectives to aim for and anti-goals to avoid. Rendered after Brand. Optional.

contentAnchors.description: Real content anchors — actual names, labels, items the design must use, not lorem. Rendered after Design direction. Optional.

constraints.description: Hard constraints: deadlines, compliance, offline, etc.

outOfScope.description: What the client explicitly said this app is NOT.

layoutTemplate.description: The Layout Template picked at intake (vocabulary: Layout Template, Named Container, Rung): category from the closed list, archetype from the six-archetype gallery, copied VERBATIM from layout_templates.json — never composed or edited at intake. Optional; omit when the client declines.

flows.description: The user journeys, wiring declared surfaces into linear chains. Optional: when absent the engine DERIVES one draft flow per shell, marked provenance inferred — confirm with `appbox intake flows confirm`.

personas.description: The user types the client named — VARIABLE N, as many as they have. Optional and ABSENT on every project created before Slice B, which must keep emitting: absent yields personas.json = [], never an error. Do NOT derive these from `audience`: that field is one JTBD sentence with no name, role or goals, so a persona built from it would be invention wearing the authority of elicitation (§22). Never padded to three — a padded persona is indistinguishable from an elicited one once it is on a card.

map.description: Where appbox-story-mapper DEPOSITS its story map: {releases, epics[{name, features[{name, stories[{name, priority, release}]}]}]}. Intake does not elicit this and does not own it — it republishes it to intake/map.json with content-derived ids and counts baked in. Shape: skills/appbox-story-mapper/story-map.schema.json. Declared here because this schema is additionalProperties:false at the top level, so an answers document carrying the group would otherwise be schema-illegal while the Dart validator accepted it — silent drift between the two.

moodboard.description: Where appbox-moodboarder DEPOSITS its moodboard: {provenance (free-text method), boards[{id, title, slice, informs, references[...]}]}. Republished to intake/moodboard.json with shot id/src precomputed. Shape: skills/appbox-moodboarder/moodboard.schema.json. Declared here for the same reason as `map`.

surfaces.description: The registry seed — what the client wants named. surface is ALWAYS null in a seed: intake names, it never designs (§22). comp is derived by convention at emit time, never authored here.

provenance.description: Who supplied this field. 'inferred' = NOT elicited; a placeholder the brief must visibly flag. There is no fourth value — 'guessed', 'assumed', 'default' are all 'inferred'.

persona.description: One user type, as the client described them. Slice B2.

id.description: DERIVED at emit time as `persona-<slug(name)>` — do not author it. An explicit id still wins, the same override story_map.dart allows a feature to pin its surface id.

name.description: What the client calls this user type, in their words. Must be unique: two personas with the same name derive the same id and one would shadow the other.

contexts.description: Where and when they use it ('phone between meetings').

proficiency.description: Deliberately NOT a closed vocabulary. `states` is closed because a gate matches on it; nothing matches on proficiency, and a three-word scale invented here would reject a client who said 'power user'.

accessibility.description: Access needs the client stated. Absent means unstated, which must not be read as 'none'.

adjectives.description: Words the design should feel like.

avoids.description: Anti-goals — what the design must NOT feel like.

areas.description: CSS grid-template-areas per rung of the viewport ladder (compact 390 / medium 744 / expanded 1280); each array item is one quoted row.

containers.description: Named Container sidecar: container name (closed vocabulary) -> {type, hints}.

id.description: <shell>.<short>, lowercase dotted, permanent (declare-structure naming). Renaming breaks every downstream reference.

shell.description: The shell group this surface belongs to; MUST equal the id's first segment.

route.description: Optional route override (e.g. /product/:id). Omit — the engine derives /<short> by convention.

requiresAuth.description: Optional: the screen sits behind sign-in. Carried into the registry when true (additive).

tab.description: Optional: bottom-tab membership (the scaffolder's shell group). Carried into the registry when true (additive).

states.description: Optional per-surface states. CONTRACT PAIR: this enum is the same closed set, in the same order, as `surfaceStates` in appboxd/lib/intake.dart, which is what actually rejects a synonym — nothing loads this schema, so drift here is invisible. Closed on purpose: an open list let every project invent 'skeleton'/'pending'/'blank' that no kit implements. Carried into the registry seed as an additive key when non-empty.

edge.description: One transition in a flow. CONTRACT PAIR: this property set is the same closed set as `edgeKeys` in appboxd/lib/intake.dart, which is what actually rejects unknown keys — nothing loads this schema, so drift here is invisible. Change both together, or emitted flows.json will violate its own published schema (it already did for `element` and `feedback`).

trigger.description: The user gesture or system event that takes this edge, in the client's words.

action.description: Typed nav op (default push). system = non-gesture edge (auth-success, deep-link) — a route guard downstream, never a button.

element.description: OPTIONAL. The thing a user touches to take this edge, joining to a `data-el` value on the surface (e.g. "button:Continue"). It exists because `trigger` is prose written for a human reader. The flow-walk island matches this EXACTLY and falls back to a fuzzy `trigger` match when it is absent, so omitting it degrades matching rather than breaking the flow. Never derived — guessing which button an edge fires is generation (§22).

feedback.description: OPTIONAL. The toast this transition fires. It lives on the EDGE and never in a screen's `states`, because a toast is a consequence of moving, not a way a screen can look (maps to kit/ui_library; `states` maps to kit/state).

kind.description: Closed set. The renderer derives the tick/styling from this — the text never carries them.

text.description: The words the user actually reads. When intake DERIVES a feedback it copies the trigger verbatim and stamps `inferred: true`; rewriting the trigger into nicer copy would be generation (§22).

inferred.description: Present and true only on a feedback intake derived rather than elicited. The confirm step exists to strike it.

action.description: OPTIONAL. The button ON the toast — a snackbar's defining feature (a recoverable error with a Retry is core snackbar material, which is why `error` is a legitimate kind). NOT the same thing as the edge's own `action`, which is the typed nav op. CONTRACT PAIR with `feedbackActionKeys` in appboxd/lib/intake.dart. Never derived — inventing a button the client did not ask for is generation (§22).

label.description: The words on the button, e.g. "Retry".

trigger.description: What taking it does, in the client's words — same prose vocabulary as the edge's `trigger`, and deliberately NOT a surface id: the canonical case (Retry) re-runs the failed operation rather than navigating anywhere.

edges.description: A LINEAR chain: <=1 outgoing and <=1 incoming edge per screen. No branches, loops or self-edges; a screen may appear in many flows.
